nodes.name: Run Tick Now
nodes.notes:
The same three jobs, on demand. Two reasons it exists beyond convenience:

1. It makes the queue behaviour DEMONSTRABLE. Edge cases 9 and 10 are about what
   happens on the next tick, and a reviewer should not have to wait five minutes
   per assertion to watch them.
2. It is what an operator wants at 4pm on a Friday after fixing a credential -
   "drain the backlog now" rather than "wait and hope".

responseMode onReceived: it answers 200 immediately and keeps working, because
the caller wants an acknowledgement, not a report. The report is LP-07.

nodes.name: Read Due Jobs
nodes.notes:
The due comparison is pushed into the store rather than done in code, so a
growing queue does not mean a growing read. The `lte` operator was verified
against this instance's Data Table API before it was relied on (it validates
server-side and rejects a type mismatch) - see 05_Test_Evidence.

nodes.name: Claim Batch
nodes.notes:
Returning [] on an empty queue ends the branch silently. A scheduled workflow that
logs "nothing to do" every 5 minutes buries the runs that did something.

nodes.name: Mark In Flight
nodes.notes:
Claim before work, the same rule as everywhere else. Two ticks overlapping - which
happens the moment one run takes longer than the interval - would otherwise both
read the same pending rows and send every follow-up twice.

nodes.name: Send Follow-up

value.context_json: ={{ JSON.stringify({ lead: $json.lead, score: $json.lead.score, band: $json.lead.band, odoo_lead_id: $json.lead.odoo_lead_id, missing: "" }) }}

nodes.notes:
Waited on, unlike most sub-workflow calls here, because the job row has to record
what actually happened. `job_id` is passed so LP-92 can re-read the queue row and
refuse to send a job that was cancelled between this claim and the send.

nodes.name: Escalate SLA
nodes.notes:
`to` is intentionally not a real address here: sla_breach is a manager-audience
template, and LP-92 addresses manager mail from lp_config rather than from the
caller. Routing an escalation through the same send gate keeps it inside the same
idempotency and audit story as everything else - one breach, one alert, however
many ticks observe it.

value.detail_json: ={{ JSON.stringify({ template: $json.template, result: $json.result, attempts: $json.attempts, overdue_by_seconds: $json.overdue_by, deferred_to_next_tick: $json.deferred }) }}

nodes.name: Read Stuck Jobs
nodes.notes:
A job claimed more than 15 minutes ago and never completed means the tick that
claimed it died. Without this scan those rows sit in `inflight` forever and the
follow-up is simply never sent - the quietest possible failure, and the reason
claim-based queues need a reaper.

nodes.name: Read Stale Claims
nodes.notes:
EDGE CASE 7, the safety net behind the safety net. LP-03 already searches Odoo by
external key before every create, so a lost acknowledgement is normally repaired
on the next attempt. This catches the case where there IS no next attempt because
the execution died and nothing retried it.

nodes.name: Read Active Leads
nodes.notes:
executeOnce is load-bearing, not tidiness. The node upstream emits one item per
agent, and a Data Table read runs once per input item - so without this the whole
owner-health branch ran four times over. It reassigned the same lead four times,
wrote four identical audit rows, sent four writes to Odoo, and counted every
salesperson's workload at four times its real value, which pushed the team over
capacity and dropped assignment to the fallback rung. Found by reading the audit
log after EC-9 failed: four rows saying "mgr-01 -> mgr-01" is not a routing bug,
it is the same routing decision made four times.

nodes.name: Reassign Lead
nodes.notes:
Every column is remapped from the row that was just read, because the Data Table
node upserts whole rows and has no partial update. Reading the full row first is
what makes that safe - the two other fields are the only ones that change.

nodes.name: Reassign in Odoo
nodes.notes:
The CRM has to agree, or the salesperson opening Odoo still sees the old owner and
the reassignment exists only in our own table. Not waited on: a failed CRM write
here raises its own dead letter and the local record is already correct.

value.detail_json: ={{ JSON.stringify({ reason: $json.reason, previous_owner_state: $json.previous_owner_state, rung: $json.assign_rung, trigger: "owner health scan" }) }}

parameters.content:
## LP-04 Tick - every 5 minutes, three jobs

**A. Drain the due queue.** Follow-ups and SLA timers are rows with a `due_at`, not Wait nodes - which is the only reason cancellation works: a held-open Wait cannot be cancelled cleanly and does not survive a restart. Batch capped at 25; the rest wait for the next tick. **(EC-10)**

**B. Self-heal.** Jobs stuck `inflight` for 15 min (a tick died mid-batch) are requeued, 3 strikes then failed. CRM claims stuck `claimed` for 10 min are dead-lettered for the replay path rather than retried here - two recovery mechanisms would eventually disagree. **(EC-7)**

**C. Owner health.** A salesperson going unavailable errors nothing, so nothing notices. The scan finds their leads, reassigns them across the team, and writes it to Odoo too. **(EC-9)**

5 minutes, not 1: the smallest window that matters is the 30-minute SLA.
